chunks: From him, from al-Nadr, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Mada'ini, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The price of wine is among the consumption of khums (one-fifth),' and he forbade the price of the dog.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the price of wine and dogs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) classifies the price of wine as 'akl al-suh't' (consumption of khums), indicating that the one-fifth tax is effectively 'eaten' or consumed by the seller due to the impurity of the commodity. He further extends this principle by specifically forbidding the price of a dog, highlighting the broader juristic concern with the monetary value of impure or distinctively categorized items in commercial transactions.
